title: Audience
description: The front matter of an audience under .ai/repo/why/audiences/: who recognises a set of operational moments, and how they work. The body carries the narrative (## Who this is, ## How they work, ## What goes wrong). An audience never lists its moments: membership is declared by each moment's `audiences`, and the list, the count and the ordering are derived from that.

schema.description: The format version of this record. A version the tool does not know is refused, never guessed.

id.description: The identity and the slug. It fixes the file name and the route /why/audiences/<id>/.

title.description: Who they are, in the words they would use.

short_title.description: Two or three words for a filter chip. Absent means the title is used.

summary.description: One line: what the working situation is. Also the page description.

workflow.description: One line: how work actually flows for them, which is what decides which moments they meet.

status.description: stable: complete and public, and held to the coverage floor. draft: written and not yet complete; listed as a draft, never counted. deprecated: kept because its route exists, listed nowhere.

weight.description: Presentation order within a listing, lowest first.
